title: Writing a Membrane Address for Akt

scenes.visual: Schematic cross-section of a muscle cell edge filling 65% of the frame height: extracellular space above, plasma membrane bilayer across the upper middle, cytosol below, marked 'schematic'. Establish the shared colour map carried across both films: warm amber (#F59E0B) insulin and receptor, soft teal (#2DD4BF) IRS-1, sky blue (#38BDF8) PI 3-kinase, slate-blue (#64748B) PIP2, bright gold (#FACC15) PIP3, yellow-white (#FEF08A) phosphate badges, muted coral (#FB7185) folded Akt turning bright coral-red (#F43F5E) when active, violet (#A78BFA) PDK1, lavender (#C4B5FD) mTORC2. Molecules drift slowly as the title appears: Writing a Membrane Address for Akt.

scenes.tts: Insulin never crosses the cell membrane, yet muscle cells pull in glucose within minutes. How does a hormone outside wake up an enzyme drifting deep inside the cell? The cell solves this problem by writing a temporary lipid address on its inner membrane.
scenes.caption: Insulin never crosses the cell membrane, yet muscle cells pull in glucose within minutes. How does a hormone outside wake up an enzyme drifting deep inside the cell? The cell solves this problem by writing a temporary lipid address on its inner membrane.
scenes.visual: Warm amber insulin molecules drift in the extracellular space above the bilayer, bouncing gently off the outer leaflet to show they do not cross. Below in the cytosol, muted coral folded Akt drifts idly, labelled 'Akt (inactive)'. A faint dotted outline highlights a patch of the inner leaflet labelled 'membrane address?'.
scenes.narration: Insulin never crosses the cell membrane, yet muscle cells pull in glucose within minutes. How does a hormone outside wake up an enzyme drifting deep inside the cell? The cell solves this problem by writing a temporary lipid address on its inner membrane.

scenes.tts: Amber insulin docks onto its receptor spanning the bilayer. The receptor is a tyrosine kinase. It adds phosphates to its own tyrosines, then marks a nearby docking protein, I R S one. Those fresh phosphotyrosines turn the docking protein into a busy landing pad.
scenes.caption: Amber insulin docks onto its receptor spanning the bilayer. The receptor is a tyrosine kinase. It adds phosphates to its own tyrosines, then marks a nearby docking protein, IRS-1. Those fresh phosphotyrosines turn the docking protein into a busy landing pad.
scenes.visual: Amber insulin locks into the extracellular jaws of the transmembrane receptor. The intracellular receptor tails glow and acquire yellow-white 'P' badges on tyrosines, then transfer 'P' badges along the tail of the soft teal IRS-1 block anchored beside the receptor. Label 'IRS-1' appears at full contrast.
scenes.narration: Amber insulin docks onto its receptor spanning the bilayer. The receptor is a tyrosine kinase. It adds phosphates to its own tyrosines, then marks a nearby docking protein, IRS-1. Those fresh phosphotyrosines turn the docking protein into a busy landing pad.

scenes.tts: Now P I three kinase arrives from the cytosol. Its regulatory subunit grips those phosphotyrosines using S H two domains. Docking pulls the enzyme against the bilayer and loosens its regulatory brake. The catalytic subunit adds one phosphate at position three of the lipid's ring-shaped head. Membrane lipid P I P two, carrying two phosphates, becomes gold P I P three, carrying three.
scenes.caption: Now PI 3-kinase arrives from the cytosol. Its regulatory subunit grips those phosphotyrosines using SH2 domains. Docking pulls the enzyme against the bilayer and loosens its regulatory brake. The catalytic subunit adds one phosphate at position 3 of the lipid's ring-shaped head. Membrane lipid PIP2, carrying two phosphates, becomes gold PIP3, carrying three.
scenes.visual: A two-block sky blue PI 3-kinase (smaller regulatory block gripping a larger catalytic block) glides up to teal IRS-1. Its notched SH2 pockets snap onto the 'P' badges on IRS-1; the regulatory block pivots slightly open to uncover the catalytic site. Adjacent slate-blue PIP2 tiles in the inner leaflet flip one by one into glowing bright gold PIP3 tiles with a '3-P' badge, labelled 'PIP2 -> PIP3'. Empathy fix: As the tiles flip, inset the lipid's ring-shaped head with positions 3, 4 and 5 numbered; a new P lands on position 3, labelled 'PIP2 (P on 4, 5)' → 'PIP3 (P on 3, 4, 5)'.
scenes.narration: Now PI 3-kinase arrives from the cytosol. Its regulatory subunit grips those phosphotyrosines using SH2 domains. Docking pulls the enzyme against the bilayer and loosens its regulatory brake. The catalytic subunit adds one phosphate at position 3 of the lipid's ring-shaped head. Membrane lipid PIP2, carrying two phosphates, becomes gold PIP3, carrying three.

scenes.tts: That gold lipid patch is the membrane address for Akt. Before insulin arrives, Akt drifts folded and quiet in the cytosol. Its folded shape keeps its activation loop hidden. Akt carries a lipid-binding P H domain at one end. When the gold patch appears, that pocket grips it and anchors Akt.
scenes.caption: That gold lipid patch is the membrane address for Akt. Before insulin arrives, Akt drifts folded and quiet in the cytosol. Its folded shape keeps its activation loop hidden. Akt carries a lipid-binding PH domain at one end. When the gold patch appears, that pocket grips it and anchors Akt.
scenes.visual: Zoom gently onto the glowing gold PIP3 patch while keeping the receptor and IRS-1 softly visible to the left. Muted coral folded Akt rises from the cytosol, its rounded PH pocket snapping cleanly onto a gold PIP3 head group. Label 'PH domain' highlights the grip as Akt locks onto the inner membrane.
scenes.narration: That gold lipid patch is the membrane address for Akt. Before insulin arrives, Akt drifts folded and quiet in the cytosol. Its folded shape keeps its activation loop hidden. Akt carries a lipid-binding PH domain at one end. When the gold patch appears, that pocket grips it and anchors Akt.

scenes.tts: Binding the lipid also unfolds Akt, exposing its activation loop. A second kinase, P D K one, sits nearby on the lipid through its own P H domain. P D K one phosphorylates that loop. Another kinase complex, m T O R C two, marks Akt's tail.
scenes.caption: Binding the lipid also unfolds Akt, exposing its activation loop. A second kinase, PDK1, sits nearby on the lipid through its own PH domain. PDK1 phosphorylates that loop. Another kinase complex, mTORC2, marks Akt's tail.
scenes.visual: As coral Akt grips gold PIP3, its folded hinge swings open to reveal an internal loop labelled 'Thr308'. Violet PDK1, already anchored on a neighbouring gold PIP3 via its own PH pocket, leans over and stamps a bright yellow-white 'P' onto Thr308. Lavender mTORC2 docks beside the tail and stamps a second 'P' onto 'Ser473'. Akt transitions to bright coral-red with a pulsing active halo. Empathy fix: Label it 'mTORC2 (a kinase)'.
scenes.narration: Binding the lipid also unfolds Akt, exposing its activation loop. A second kinase, PDK1, sits nearby on the lipid through its own PH domain. PDK1 phosphorylates that loop. Another kinase complex, mTORC2, marks Akt's tail.

scenes.tts: The loop phosphate does most of the work, and the tail phosphate adds full power. Keep this rule in mind. P I P three recruits Akt to the membrane, where two phosphates activate it. Here, the upstream steps write that address when insulin arrives.
scenes.caption: The loop phosphate does most of the work, and the tail phosphate adds full power. Keep this rule in mind. PIP3 recruits Akt to the membrane, where two phosphates activate it. Here, the upstream steps write that address when insulin arrives.
scenes.visual: Hold the active membrane assembly as a clean left-to-right animated pulse travels along it: amber receptor -> teal IRS-1 -> sky blue PI 3-kinase -> gold PIP3 -> bright coral-red Akt carrying two 'P' badges (Thr308 and Ser473). Keep labels crisp, at most 5 words each, with slow ambient motion.
scenes.narration: The loop phosphate does most of the work, and the tail phosphate adds full power. Keep this rule in mind. PIP3 recruits Akt to the membrane, where two phosphates activate it. Here, the upstream steps write that address when insulin arrives.

scenes.tts: Let us test that rule with a drug. Suppose a drug blocks the catalytic subunit of P I three kinase. Insulin still binds, and the receptor still marks I R S one. Will Akt still gain its activating phosphates?
scenes.caption: Let us test that rule with a drug. Suppose a drug blocks the catalytic subunit of PI 3-kinase. Insulin still binds, and the receptor still marks IRS-1. Will Akt still gain its activating phosphates?
scenes.visual: Reset the same cell-edge scene with amber insulin docked and teal IRS-1 carrying 'P' badges. Sky blue PI 3-kinase is docked on IRS-1 but its catalytic block carries an X mark ('drug-blocked'). Slate PIP2 tiles stay slate. Muted coral folded Akt drifts in the cytosol; violet PDK1 waits nearby. Question overlay fades in at the bottom: 'PI 3-kinase blocked + insulin: does Akt get phosphorylated?'.
scenes.narration: Let us test that rule with a drug. Suppose a drug blocks the catalytic subunit of PI 3-kinase. Insulin still binds, and the receptor still marks IRS-1. Will Akt still gain its activating phosphates?

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause: keep the question card on screen while the X-marked PI 3-kinase sits on IRS-1, slate PIP2 tiles remain unchanged, and folded Akt drifts slowly in the cytosol below.

scenes.tts: No, activation fails. The receptor and docking protein still light up, but no gold lipid appears. With no address, Akt stays folded in the cytosol, far from P D K one. Without the lipid, phosphorylation fails.
scenes.caption: No, activation fails. The receptor and docking protein still light up, but no gold lipid appears. With no address, Akt stays folded in the cytosol, far from PDK1. Without the lipid, phosphorylation fails.
scenes.visual: The receptor and IRS-1 keep their 'P' badges, but no slate tile turns gold. Folded coral Akt drifts below the membrane without docking, carrying no 'P' badges. A crisp status label reads 'No PIP3: Akt stays off'.
scenes.narration: No, activation fails. The receptor and docking protein still light up, but no gold lipid appears. With no address, Akt stays folded in the cytosol, far from PDK1. Without the lipid, phosphorylation fails.

scenes.tts: Requiring a membrane lipid and two separate kinases works like a safety lock. Akt turns on mainly where active receptors build three-phosphorylated lipids, and while those lipids last. Put together, lipid docking and dual phosphorylation switch Akt on cleanly.
scenes.caption: Requiring a membrane lipid and two separate kinases works like a safety lock. Akt turns on mainly where active receptors build 3-phosphorylated lipids, and while those lipids last. Put together, lipid docking and dual phosphorylation switch Akt on cleanly.
scenes.visual: Restore normal coral Akt locking onto gold PIP3, unfolding, and lighting up with both 'P' badges (Thr308 and Ser473) as three subtle checkmarks tick on beside '1. PIP3', '2. Thr308-P', '3. Ser473-P'. Smooth fade toward the end card.
scenes.narration: Requiring a membrane lipid and two separate kinases works like a safety lock. Akt turns on mainly where active receptors build 3-phosphorylated lipids, and while those lipids last. Put together, lipid docking and dual phosphorylation switch Akt on cleanly.

scenes.visual: Clean end card showing one line only, centred at large high-contrast type with no smaller line underneath: 'PIP3 recruits Akt to the membrane, where two phosphates activate it.'
